exposure: Early childhood medication exposure (antiinfectives for systemic use, respiratory system drugs, sensory organ drugs, antibiotics, antipyretic/anti-inflammatory medication)
Perinatal factors (premature birth, mode of delivery)
cohort: 298,502 children between 6 and 9 years of age were identified from claims data of a major national health insurance company in Germany, categorized into MIH and unaffected control groups.
finding: Significantly larger prescription quantities of antiinfectives, respiratory system drugs, and sensory organ drugs, particularly antibiotics, were found in the first 4 years of life for children with MIH compared to unaffected individuals, while no association was found for premature birth, mode of delivery, or antipyretic/anti-inflammatory medication.
mod_finding: No association was found between mode of delivery and Molar Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH).
followup_time: Up to 9 years of age (for outcome assessment)
